name: 2018 information-economy geography telemetry heuristic
caveats: A 2018 heuristic for historical pattern review; it concerns historical patterns rather than current presence or person/company attribution.
Keep raw IP ranges and network selectors from the article out of a public people database.
The named countries, cities, universities, networks, and providers remain contextual references rather than implicated entities.
Foreign contractors, customers, local companies, schools, universities, jurisdictions, networks, and service providers require direct evidence before treatment as knowing participants.
Geographic traffic patterns are contextual; identity, nationality, employer, sanctions status, and wrongdoing require source corroboration.

The telemetry method, period and information-economy/manual-labor distinction are historical context; country overlap supplies contextual similarity, while later-reporting linkage requires a source bridge.
This is a historical, source-qualified program-level finding; current census and person, organization, jurisdiction, platform-user or technology-user status require current sources.

infrastructure.statement: Using third-party network data, IP geolocation, routing data, and open-source information for March-August 2018, Recorded Future assessed that China, India, Nepal, Bangladesh, Mozambique, Kenya, Thailand, and Indonesia were more likely than Russia to host North Koreans working in service or information-economy roles. The report observed regional activity in China and India and contrasted an internet-dependent, customer-facing model—such as building games, applications, bots, and other IT products—with predominantly manual overseas labor.
infrastructure.evidence_class: network-telemetry and open-source heuristic covering March 16-August 30, 2018
infrastructure.historical_boundary: A 2018 heuristic, not a current presence assessment and not person- or company-level attribution.
